Profile Interleukin-10 is one of a number of polypeptides known collec- tively as interleukins (p.2325). It regulates the differentiation and proliferation of several immune cells including T-cells and B- cells. It is postulated that it has immunostimulant as well as im- munosuppressive properties; it also has anti-inflammatory ac- tions. Interleukin-10 is under investigation for inflammatory bowel disease, malignant neoplasms, skin disorders including psoriasis and reduction of scarring, rheumatoid arthritis, hepatitis C, and organ transplantation. Ilodecakin is a recombinant form of interleukin-10 under inves- tigation. ◊ References. 1. Asadullah K, et al. Interleukin-10 therapy—review of a new ap- proach. Pharmacol Rev 2003; 55: 241–69. 2.
